info.title: WG-Guard API
info.description:
REST management surface of the WG-Guard AmneziaWG node panel. Technical templates are available at /api/v1/templates and referenced by template_id; they are not external sales products. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer wg_…` API tokens (scopes below). Reseller-bound tokens use ownership-checked routes and owner-assigned templates; direct purchase terms require an owner-scoped token. All errors use one envelope (`error.code` is a stable machine code). Ordinary mutating endpoints with `Idempotency-Key` use token-scoped 24-hour response replay; they do not gain atomic multi-request semantics or result lookup. Purchases and quota top-ups commit their mutation and a non-secret result together; `Idempotency-Key` identifies that result for 90 days within the owner or reseller namespace. Lists are cursor-paginated (`limit` ≤ 500 + opaque `cursor`).

Units: quotas, charged usage and resource sizes are exact bytes (B); panel MB/GB are decimal (1 GB = 1000000000 B). Send 100000000000 for 100 GB; 107374182400 is 100 GiB and displays as 107.4 GB. Speed limits use decimal Kbps (1000 bits/s): Mbps × 1000, panel MB/s × 8000. Download is server to client; upload is client to server. RX is server received (client upload); TX is server sent (client download); both directions consume quota. Telemetry *_bytes_per_second is B/s, not Kbps. Durations/cadence/uptime are seconds; 30 days = 2592000 s and panel month shortcuts mean 30 days. Date-time fields are RFC3339 instants; responses use UTC (Z). Webhook signature t uses Unix seconds, not milliseconds. Utilization is percent on a 0-100 scale; load_1 is a dimensionless one-minute load average. Device limits, entity/sample counts and delivery attempts are integer counts; MTU is bytes and listen_port is a UDP port number. JSON numbers use their field's unit; conversion and display rounding never change stored quantities. See /docs for examples and settings-unit guidance.

post.summary: Provision a customer, requested devices and subscription link atomically
post.description: Requires an Idempotency-Key unique within the owner or reseller namespace. Send exactly one of template_id (technical template) or entitlement (direct finite terms). Direct terms are allowed only for owner-scoped tokens; reseller tokens must use an enabled owner-assigned template. Sales SKUs and prices live in the caller, not this catalog. An identical retry returns the same 201 result with Idempotency-Replayed: true; a different request with that key returns 409. An omitted username is derived stably from the principal and key. Database commit does not assert a successful live VPN handshake. The result contains no capability link or private configuration; retrieve those separately with appropriate permissions. device_count defaults to 1, accepts 1-100 and must fit the account device limit; it does not default to the device cap. Each device has independent keys and an allocated address. Any device failure rolls back the entire transaction, including the account, link and operation result. A successful result includes device_ids; configs/QRs remain separate no-store reads.

patch.summary: Partially update a user (username immutable; `null` clears a limit)
patch.description: Changing template_id on an existing user changes its reference only; it does not reset the existing entitlement. Update quota/duration fields explicitly or queue a successor.

delete.summary: Soft-delete a user (username stays reserved; peers removed)

get.summary: Retrieve a customer's private subscription link
get.description: The path is a bearer capability relative to this panel's public origin. Resolve it against the configured public base URL or the API origin before delivery. The link and device configurations are secrets; the response is no-store. Reseller tokens can read only their own customers. A missing or revoked link returns 404.

post.summary: Revoke the old link and every old device configuration
post.description: Atomically replaces the customer link and every device key, preserving device IDs, addresses and quotas. Old links, configs and QR values stop working after successful runtime reconciliation. If reconciliation fails, the new database state is retained and the response is 503; read the current link before retrying. This operation intentionally does not use response-replay middleware.

200.description: New private link and count of rotated devices

503.description: Database rotation committed; runtime reconciliation pending

get.description: Returns null when no successor is queued. Reseller tokens can read only their own customers.

put.summary: Queue or replace one authorized successor
put.description: No payment is taken. The caller must have already authorized this entitlement. Template terms are snapshotted when queued, so later catalog edits or reseller-template revocation do not rewrite it. At the first time or quota boundary the successor subscription starts once, with fresh usage counters. A manual suspension/disable blocks automatic activation. A changed current template or incompatible device set moves the queue to needs_review. Optional carry_unused_traffic adds only unused prior traffic when time ends first, never time. Reseller tokens require an owner-assigned enabled template. Optional Idempotency-Key provides token-scoped 24-hour replay.

delete.description: Idempotent removal; it does not reverse an already activated plan. Optional Idempotency-Key provides token-scoped 24-hour replay.

get.description: Returns newest first, at most 100, retained for one year. Includes non-secret before/after entitlement snapshots and the actual first boundary trigger. Reseller tokens see only their own customers. This read is the fallback when an asynchronous notification is missed.

post.description: Idempotent with `Idempotency-Key`. Reactivates expired accounts; traffic_exceeded accounts are NOT reactivated here (quota recovery is an explicit admin action).

duration_seconds.description: Duration in seconds: 86400 = 1 day; 2592000 = 30 days. The panel month shortcut means 30 days, not a calendar month.

exact.description: RFC3339 instant with an explicit timezone (for example 2026-10-30T12:00:00Z); responses use UTC (Z). Not a localized calendar date or Unix milliseconds.

post.summary: Add paid data allowance without resetting usage
post.description: Requires an Idempotency-Key (1–128 printable ASCII characters without spaces). Atomically increases an existing finite quota and stores a before/after result for 90 days in the owner or reseller namespace; an identical retry returns the same operation with Idempotency-Replayed: true, while a different request with the key returns 409. Reseller tokens may top up only owned customers. Charged RX/TX usage stays unchanged, and manual disable/suspension is not lifted. A quota-only traffic_exceeded block is lifted when the new limit exceeds charged usage. A 503 after commit means runtime reconciliation is pending; recover the committed result through GET /api/v1/operations/result and retry with the same key. Unlimited accounts require an explicit finite limit via PATCH /users/{id}; /traffic/add is a charged-counter correction, not a top-up.

200.description: Committed top-up and before/after snapshot; same result on replay

post.summary: Add traffic to the charged counters
post.description: Idempotent with `Idempotency-Key`. Pushing the total to/over the limit trips the account immediately.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Lookback window in hours, not seconds: 24 means the preceding 24 hours. Capped by retention (samples 48, hourly 720, daily 8760).

name.description: Trimmed non-blank device label, at most 64 UTF-8 bytes. Not an idempotency/uniqueness key.

preshared_key.description: Generate an additional preshared key server-side when true; not a caller-supplied secret.

post.description: Creates one independent device/peer. Disabled devices also consume device_limit slots; creation at/over the cap returns 409 DEVICE_LIMIT_REACHED. Profile selection is explicit interface_id, user profile, then the first enabled interface in name order. The account must be enabled and peer-eligible. This route has no idempotency replay middleware: inspect the device list after a lost response before retrying. Reseller-bound tokens cannot use this write route; provision ready devices during /purchases instead.

delete.summary: Delete a device (IP released; peer removed)

post.description: The old peer key is revoked by reconciliation (matched by device IP), the new key is applied.

get.description: Requires configs.read; contains the private key — treat as a secret. Returns the canonical full-field configuration bytes shared by the admin and subscription downloads, ending in exactly one newline. Response headers include `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; the `Content-Disposition` filename has a short ASCII username label (up to six characters), a hyphen, and a stable eight-character device code followed by `.conf`. Optional downloads.filename_prefix/suffix each contribute at most two characters to the label. The profile-name stem is at most 15 characters.

get.summary: Client configuration as a PNG QR code
get.description: Encodes the exact canonical configuration returned by the text endpoint. Returns `image/png`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and an inline `.png` filename with the same short stem as the config download. An oversized configuration returns `INVALID_REQUEST` instead of partial image data.

get.description: The key determines units: *_gb is decimal GB; *_months is fixed 30-day periods; *_seconds, *_hours and *_days are time units; *_count and max_attempts are counts. network.client_persistent_keepalive is seconds in pinned 0/N/N-M string form. api.rate_limit_per_minute is requests per fixed 60-second window. Preset lists contain numeric strings. Values and zero semantics are validated per definition; see /docs.

patch.description: Send each setting in the unit of its key, not in the raw-byte unit of user quota fields. For example users.default_quota_gb: 100 prefills 100 GB, while a user's traffic_limit_bytes for that amount is 100000000000. A default-quota setting of 0 removes the prefill; user quota 0 is a finite zero-byte allowance. See /docs for time, count and rate-limit units.

post.description: An empty `secret` generates one and returns it exactly once. Signing: `X-WG-Signature: t=<ts>,v1=<hex hmac-sha256(secret, "<ts>.<body>")>` with a ~5-minute replay window.

Obfuscation.description: Complete supported AmneziaWG profile at the pinned revisions. Scalar-or-range values are inclusive: a scalar is a JSON integer and a true range is canonical string N-M. Enabled H1-H4 intervals must be non-zero and pairwise non-overlapping. AdvancedSecurity is intentionally unsupported.

jc.description: Junk packet count; enabled profiles require 1-128.

jmin.description: Minimum junk size; must be less than jmax.

jmax.description: Maximum junk size; must exceed jmin.

s2.description: Handshake-response padding size; s1 + 56 must not equal s2.

s3.description: Cookie-message padding size; explicit advanced option.

s4.description: Transport-message padding size; explicit advanced option.

h4.description: Inclusive u32 magic-header scalar or range.

i1.description: Canonical single-line UTF-8 signature value; leading/trailing whitespace and control characters are rejected.

i2.description: Canonical single-line UTF-8 signature value; leading/trailing whitespace and control characters are rejected.

max_handshake_attempts.description: Inclusive u16 maximum-handshake-attempt scalar or range; zero uses the backend default.

listen_port.description: UDP port number, not a byte or time quantity.

ipv4_subnet.description: IPv4 network in CIDR notation; the prefix after / is a bit count (for example 10.8.0.0/24).

preset.description: Persisted profile classification; custom is inferred when explicit parameters are supplied.

post.description: The configured endpoint receives an at-least-once POST. Return any 2xx to acknowledge; other statuses and transport failures are retried. Deduplicate by body `id`. Delivery may reorder, including across endpoints. A reseller receiver receives only events belonging to its reseller; node.started is node-wide only. A node-wide receiver gets reseller events only after an explicit owner opt-in; existing receivers migrate with that option off.

parameters.name: X-WG-Delivery
parameters.description: Stable delivery ID for this endpoint and event.

parameters.name: X-WG-Signature
parameters.description: t=<unix_seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, '<t>.<raw body>')>. Reject timestamps outside a five-minute replay window.

x-webhooks.description: Events and one pending delivery per subscribed enabled receiver commit with the mutation. Scheduler polls every 5 s, takes up to 64 due deliveries per pass, with up to four concurrent 10 s HTTP requests. Non-2xx and network failures retry after 30 s doubling to a 6 h cap; after webhooks.max_attempts (default 12) the delivery is dead until manually redeliverable. Retention is seven days. Crash after HTTP success but before the SQLite receipt update can duplicate a POST; receivers deduplicate by event id. There is no total, per-user, or cross-endpoint delivery ordering guarantee. Use resource GET and the scoped receipt API to reconcile state. Node-wide endpoints receive reseller events only with explicit owner opt-in.
